scope: Authenticate the project MAME host window and test a bounded pointer path for the GTK2 horizontal held-state comparison, then restore the host and MAME input state.

host_window_intervention.method: X11 window was authenticated by _NET_WM_PID, then briefly activated to capture only that MAME window.
host_window_intervention.restoration: A KWin script's scheduled restoration did not occur as expected. I detected the active window state and explicitly minimized the authenticated MAME XID; final WM_STATE was Iconic, _NET_WM_STATE was HIDDEN, and _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW returned to 0. The script was no longer loaded.

capture_off_test.movement: One host-pixel move from (600,100) to (601,100), no button.
capture_off_test.result: With the existing hook released, direct host motion produced no guest-frame difference.

hook_recapture_test.method: One left click at local MAME-client coordinate (900,200), a blank blue desktop area away from controls. The existing hook had capture=false and had disabled guest mouse sequences; its own transition consumed the click and re-enabled input after button-up.
hook_recapture_test.movement: One host-pixel move from (1460,260) to (1461,260), no button.
hook_recapture_test.interpretation: No pointer was visible in either capture and no arrow target could be confirmed. The four changed pixels fall in the bottom-panel clock area; they do not identify pointer motion. This is inconclusive, not proof that guest input did not move the pointer.

result: The project window is now authenticated and can be captured independently. Direct host motion while released is ignored; after the existing hook recaptures, a one-pixel motion did not expose a cursor in the guest capture. The cursor was therefore not safely locatable over a scrollbar arrow, and no arrow was pressed.
next: Continue I167/GTK2 only. Preserve this corrected host-window identity and the explicit cleanup sequence. Do not repeat counter deltas or infer a guest cursor from host coordinates; inspect a cursor-visible MAME/guest capture path before any held-arrow input.
